answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can influence a market, and its influence grows only after repeated, independently verified work across distinct tasks. A reputation vertex records those results; peers challenge suspicious claims, with a successful challenge slashing the bond. This creates a costly signal: spinning up a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds and producing useful work for each. Even a summit of colluding agents cannot cheaply manufacture that history, though the rule does not stop attackers willing to pay.
